cases.question: Any CRC errors on the router interfaces in the last 7 days?
cases.evidence: Broad: retrieve offered 20 metrics (in_crc_errors first, then ifInErrors, ifOutErrors, the telemetry in/out errors, discards, ifOperStatus and more). Cisco_IOS_XE_interfaces_oper:interfaces_interface_statistics_in_crc_errors is carried by r1, r2, r3, r4, r6, r7, r8 only (job telemetry_mdt; labels device, name, host, path, source, subscription; NO role label), 34 series at 22:24:40 UTC and 45 at 22:25:49 UTC (4, 7, 10, 6, 8, 5, 5 per router; the telemetry series churn on their discontinuity_time label). ifInErrors (counter, IF-MIB, counts CRC among input errors) carries device and role; 45 series with role router. Healthy-nothing, 22:25:49 and 22:26:29 UTC: sum(increase(in_crc_errors[7d])) = 0; max_over_time(in_crc_errors[7d]) > 0 answers no series; sum(increase(ifInErrors{role="router"}[7d])) = 0, and by device > 0 no series; sum(increase(telemetry in_errors[7d])) = 0 and in_errors_64 = 0. Every accepted metric's right answer is a flat zero.
cases.flag: The scope 'the router interfaces' is right as role router or as the seven routers r1-r4, r6-r8; the judge cannot accept either, so neither role nor devices is expected. The telemetry metrics carry no role label: a model choosing one with role router has its role dropped by the builder (all their devices are routers, so the answer is the same), while ifInErrors with no role or devices would also show the switches. IF-MIB has no CRC-only object; ifInErrors (or telemetry in_errors) is the input-error total that holds CRC, accepted as the SNMP answer. 'In the last 7 days' is the relative 7d, never this week.

cases.question: How much traffic is r2 sending out of its interfaces right now?
cases.evidence: Broad: retrieve offered 20 metrics (ifOutOctets, ifHCOutOctets, telemetry out_octets and out_octets_64 first, then packets, discards, errors and in-direction octets). ifHCOutOctets (counter, bytes) has 7 series on r2 at 22:25:49 UTC; rate(ifHCOutOctets{device="r2"}[5m]) * 8 > 0 answered 4: GigabitEthernet2 31.6 kb/s, Gi4 3.1 kb/s, Gi3 1.4 kb/s, Gi1 111 b/s. Telemetry tx_kbps on r2 at the same instant: Gi2 25 and 27 (two series), Gi3 2, Gi4 1, Gi1 0, Loopback0 0.
cases.flag: With an octet counter the first step must be a rate (the builder puts rate:5m first if none is given), and bits are a reasonable but unstated choice; tx_kbps is already a rate in kbit/s and takes no rate, so first_op is not expected. 'Right now' is a current reading: 1h is the closest chip, 24h still ends at now; per-interface or summed for r2 are both fair (one device, so a no-label sum is allowed).

Healthy-nothing at 22:25:49 UTC: sum(increase(ifOutErrors{role="switch"}[1d])) = 0; by device > 0 answers no series. The telemetry out_errors is carried by the routers only, so it cannot answer for switches.
cases.flag: Role switch and the five switches s1-s5 are the same scope; the judge accepts only role switch. Per port or summed per switch are both fair, so no group is expected; a no-label sum across the five switches would be a miss by the judge's one-line rule.

cases.question: Which 10 interfaces received the most multicast packets in the last 24 hours?
cases.evidence: Broad: retrieve offered 20 metrics (ifInMulticastPkts, ifHCInMulticastPkts, unicast, telemetry in_multicast_pkts, discards, errors, broadcast, out-direction multicast and more). ifHCInMulticastPkts (counter): 47 router and 42 switch series; ifInMulticastPkts: 47 and 47. topk(10, increase(ifHCInMulticastPkts[1d])) at 22:25:49 UTC: s2 Gi0/3 395.8k, s1 Gi0/3 187.1k, s3 Gi0/3 86.2k, s4 Gi0/3 51.9k, r8 Gi3.10 39.8k, s4 Gi0/2 22.7k, s3 Gi0/2 22.7k, s4 Gi1/0 22.6k, s3 Gi1/0 22.6k, s1 Gi0/2 6.9k; topk by rate[5m] has the same leaders (s2 Gi0/3 4.5 pkt/s). Nine of the ten are switch ports.
cases.flag: The telemetry in_multicast_pkts covers routers only, and the switch ports hold nine of the top ten, so it is not accepted. A rate shows the top ten at each step; an increase over a window is closer to 'received the most' over the day, and either is accepted (topk keeps the highest at each step, so more than ten may appear over 24 h).

cases.evidence: retrieve offered 2 metrics: ospfNbrState, ospfv3NbrState (gauges). ospfNbrState is carried by r1, r2, r3, r4, r6, r8, s3, s4 (job ospf; NOT r7, which holds no ospfNbrState or ospfv3NbrState series over 7 days); ospfv3NbrState by r1-r4, r6, r8 (job ospfv3). r6 has one neighbour in each: ospfNbrState (neighbour 10.255.4.1) = 8, full, and ospfv3NbrState (router id 184484110) = 8 at 22:25:49 and 22:26:44 UTC. Healthy-nothing over today (2026-10-26 00:00 to 22:26 UTC, a window of 80749 s and 80804 s): changes = 0 and resets = 0 for both, min_over_time = 8 for both, 1345 ospfNbrState samples in the window. No neighbour was lost.
cases.flag: OSPFv2 or OSPFv3 are both 'OSPF'; the builder takes one metric, so either is accepted, and neither alone covers both. 'Lost' is measured by changes or resets of the state (a fall from full), or by keeping the values not equal to (or below) 8, full; all are accepted as the first step. Today is From 2026-10-26 00:00 UTC to now; a 24h chip would reach into yesterday. The evidence cannot say whether the engineer counts a neighbour that never came up today as lost.

cases.question: How much memory is r3 using right now?
cases.evidence: retrieve offered 20 metrics (cempMemPoolFree, cempMemPoolName, cempMemPoolType, cempMemPoolUsed, ciscoMemoryPoolFree, ciscoMemoryPoolUsed, then the monitoring host's Telegraf mem_* with no device label). cempMemPoolUsed and ciscoMemoryPoolUsed (gauges, bytes) are carried by r1-r4, r6-r8 only (role router, job cisco_8000v), two pools per router; no switch carries a memory metric over 7 days. r3 at 00:45:36 UTC: Processor 276,337,096 bytes (cempMemPoolUsed 276,337,256), reserve Processor 88 bytes; over the last hour (read 00:46:37 UTC) Processor between 276,336,832 and 276,483,672.

cases.question: How long has r4 been up?
cases.evidence: retrieve offered 11 metrics (node_network_up, sysUpTime, sysORUpTime, ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable, node_network_carrier_up_changes_total, up, ifLastChange, ifCounterDiscontinuityTime, sysORLastChange, cbgpPeer2FsmEstablishedTime, node_softnet_received_rps_total). sysUpTime (gauge, hundredths of a second) is carried by all twelve devices, one series each. r4 at 00:54:57 UTC: 41,331,398 hundredths, 413,314 s, 4 days 18 h 48 min, so its last restart was about 2026-10-22 06:06 UTC; resets(sysUpTime{device="r4"}[7d]) = 2 at 00:46:37 UTC (one in each day-window ending 22 Oct and 23 Oct 00:00 UTC).
cases.flag: No range is stated; any is fair, the answer is the latest point. The builder has no division, so the value is read in hundredths of a second. sysORUpTime is the uptime when a MIB row was made, not the device's uptime, and up is the scrape's own health; neither is accepted. sysUpTime is the device's own counter.

cases.question: Which interfaces are down on s3?
cases.evidence: Broad: retrieve offered 20 metrics (ifAdminStatus, ifOperStatus, ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable, then 17 of the routers' telemetry interface statistics). ifOperStatus (gauge, IF-MIB: 1 up, 2 down, 7 lowerLayerDown) is carried by all twelve devices; s3 holds 10 interfaces, all 1 at 00:45:36 and 00:54:57 UTC, and ifOperStatus{device="s3"} != 1 answered no series, also at every minute of today to 00:54 UTC. Healthy-nothing for s3. Elsewhere one interface each on r6, r7 and s5 was not up at 00:54:57 UTC, so the wrong device finds something.
cases.flag: 'Down' is any state but up: ne 1 is closest; eq 2 (down) and gt 1 keep the same or a subset and are accepted. ifAdminStatus is what was configured, not whether it is down; not accepted. No range is stated; any is fair.

A count with no label puts r3 and r4 into one line, a miss by the judge's one-line rule; a count by device is fair. cbgpPeer2AdminStatus is the configured state; not accepted.

'Ports' may leave out the VLAN interfaces by a filter; fair, not judged. Bits are fair. Role switch and s1-s5 are the same scope; the judge accepts only role switch.

cases.question: Any interface errors anywhere in the network in the last hour?
cases.evidence: Broad: retrieve offered 20 metrics (ifInErrors, ifOutErrors, the telemetry in_errors, out_errors, in_crc_errors, in_errors_64, ifInDiscards, ifOutDiscards, node_textfile_scrape_error, ifIndex, ifMtu, ifNumber, ifSpeed, ifAdminStatus and more). ifInErrors and ifOutErrors (counters) are carried by all twelve devices. Healthy-nothing at 00:45:36 UTC: sum(increase(ifInErrors[1h])) = 0 and sum(increase(ifOutErrors[1h])) = 0; by device > 0 answered no series for either; the telemetry in_errors and out_errors summed = 0.
cases.flag: 'Anywhere' is all twelve devices: the telemetry errors cover the routers only and are not accepted. In or out is unstated; either is accepted. A no-label sum answers 'any' in one line but over many devices, a miss by the judge's one-line rule; per interface or by device are fair.

cases.question: How many OSPF neighbours does each router have?
cases.evidence: retrieve offered 2 metrics: ospfNbrState, ospfv3NbrState. ospfNbrState is carried by r1-r4, r6, r8 and the switches s3 and s4; at 00:45:36 UTC per router: r1 5, r2 6, r3 6, r4 7, r6 1, r8 1 (r7 none); in state 8 (full): r1 2, r2 3, r3 6, r4 7, r6 1, r8 1 (r1's other three are 4, two-way). ospfv3NbrState per router: r1 3, r2 4, r3 4, r4 5, r6 1, r8 1. With no role, s3 and s4 (5 each) would be added.
cases.flag: Whether a neighbour in two-way (a DROther's normal state) counts is the engineer's: a count by device alone, or after eq 8, are both accepted. OSPFv2 or OSPFv3 are both 'OSPF'. r7 has no neighbour, so it has no line. Role router and r1-r4, r6-r8 are the same scope; the judge accepts only role router.

cases.question: Free memory on r7 over the past week
cases.evidence: retrieve offered 20 metrics (cempMemPoolFree, ciscoMemoryPoolFree, then the monitoring host's mem_free, mem_*_free, node_memory_*Free*, go_memory_classes_*, disk_free, disk_inodes_free, cempMemPoolName, cempMemPoolType). Both are gauges in bytes, carried by the routers only. r7 at 00:45:36 UTC: Processor 1,808,521,764 bytes free (cempMemPoolFree 1,808,521,604), reserve Processor 102,316; Processor free moved by 79.8 MB over the 7 days.
cases.flag: 'The past week' is the 7d range. Per pool or summed for r7 are fair. The mem_* and node_memory_* metrics are the monitoring host's and a miss.

cases.question: Which routers had interface state changes in the last 7 days?
cases.evidence: Broad: retrieve offered 20 metrics (ifLastChange, ifAdminStatus, ifOperStatus, then 17 telemetry interface statistics including num_flaps). sum by (device) (changes(ifOperStatus{role="router"}[7d])) > 0 at 00:45:36 UTC: r6 5, r7 4 (the switches: s5 1). The telemetry num_flaps counter's increase over 7 days is 0 on every router (00:50:13 UTC) although r6 and r7 changed, so it is not accepted.
cases.flag: changes counts every state move; resets would count only the returns to up (1 is the lowest state); not accepted. ifLastChange moves when a state changes but is a time, not a state; not accepted. Per interface or summed by device are both fair. Role router and the seven routers are the same scope; the judge accepts only role router.

cases.question: Average inbound traffic per interface on r8 over the past 90 days
cases.evidence: Broad: retrieve offered 20 metrics (ifInOctets, ifHCInOctets, the telemetry in_octets, ifMtu, ifInDiscards, ifInErrors, ifOutOctets, ifHCOutOctets, in-direction packet counters and more). Prometheus keeps 90d (its storage.tsdb.retention.time, read 00:44:23 UTC), but r8's series begin 2026-10-22 23:00 UTC (the earliest timestamp of ifHCInOctets, ifInOctets and sysUpTime for r8; its telemetry in_octets from 2026-10-23 00:00 UTC); r1's begin 2026-10-01. ifHCInOctets{device="r8"}: 6 series now, 9 over 90 days; telemetry in_octets: 8 series. sum(rate(ifHCInOctets{device="r8"}[5m])) * 8 = 10.5 kb/s at 00:46:37 UTC.
cases.flag: The builder has no average over time: a per-interface rate over the 90 days, drawn as series, is the closest, with any window (1h smooths most). Per interface asks no group. The 90 days hold about 4 days of r8: the answer starts on 22 Oct, which the person should be told; a 7d or 30d range would be a different question.

cases.question: Unicast packets per second coming in on s5 today
cases.evidence: Broad: retrieve offered 20 metrics, and neither ifHCInUcastPkts nor ifInUcastPkts was among them ('unicast' is in neither name nor help; the names say Ucast and Pkts): snmp_scrape_duration_seconds, snmp_scrape_packets_*, node_network_*_packets_total, node_disk_*_time_seconds_total, the routers' telemetry in_unicast_pkts and out_unicast_pkts, scrape_duration_seconds, telemetry cpu five_seconds and more. ifHCInUcastPkts (counter) is carried by all twelve devices; s5 has 6 series (ifInUcastPkts 7). At 00:45:36 UTC rate[5m] > 0 on 4: Gi0/1 1.83 pkt/s, Vlan1 1.80, Gi0/2 0.017, Gi0/3 0.017; increase since 00:00 UTC summed 8,775 packets. The telemetry in_unicast_pkts has no s5 series (00:56:32 UTC).
cases.flag: The offer does not hold the right metrics, so a miss here may be the offer's, not the choice's. The telemetry in_unicast_pkts covers routers only (s5 is a switch): a miss. 'Per second' asks a rate. Today at this now is 57 minutes, From 2026-10-27 00:00 UTC; 1h or 24h are misses.

cases.question: What's the round-trip time on the IP SLA probes?
cases.evidence: retrieve offered 20 metrics, rttMonLatestRttOperCompletionTime first, then sysUpTime and other metrics holding 'time' (ifCounterDiscontinuityTime, sysORUpTime, node_time_*, cbgpPeer2FsmEstablishedTime, node_disk_*_time_seconds_total, diskio_*_time, kernel_boot_time). rttMonLatestRttOperCompletionTime (gauge, CISCO-RTTMON-MIB, milliseconds; job cisco_ipsla) is carried by r1 (3 operations), r2 (2), r3, r4, s2 and s3 (1 each): 9 series, roles router and switch. At 00:45:36 UTC: r1 60, 23 and 32 ms; r2 56 and 103; r3 56; r4 69; s2 46; s3 5. Highest over 24 h: 4,950 ms (r1 operation 2). rttMonLatestRttOperSense = 1 (ok) on all nine.
cases.flag: No device, role or range is expected: the probes run on six devices of both roles, and the question names none. rttMonLatestRttOperSense is the return code, not the time; a miss. No range is stated; any is fair.

cases.question: Which 5 routers are using the most memory over the last 24 hours?
cases.evidence: retrieve offered 20 metrics (as case 11). topk(5, cempMemPoolUsed) at 00:46:37 UTC: r4 276.8 MB, r3 276.3 MB, r2 270.6 MB, r1 270.3 MB, r6 270.1 MB (then r7 268.5 MB, r8 193.4 MB); topk(5, ciscoMemoryPoolUsed) the same five Processor pools; the highest over 24 h by device has the same order (r4 277.7 MB first). The reserve Processor pool is 88 bytes on each router.
cases.flag: Only the routers carry a memory metric, so role router, the seven routers or no scope give the same series; none is expected. topk over the raw pools, or over a max or sum by device, all give the same five routers. A no-label sum is one line, a miss.
